pages.title: Shoes
pages.content:
Stocked pairs

Six pairs, four lasts.

Six house pairs, each built on one or more of four lasts. Filter by N, S, W or O, then read the drop, stack, weight and price on the pair.

N · Narrow
S · Standard
W · Wide
O · Open toe

WHICH LAST?

Which last?

A last is the form a shoe is built on. We stock four, and the forefoot width is measured inside a US men's 9. Narrow, code N, is 94 mm, for low-volume feet and a narrow heel. Standard, code S, is 98 mm, and it fits most feet. Wide, code W, is 103 mm, for a high-volume foot or a wide midfoot.

Open toe, code O, is 108 mm, for a wide forefoot and for toes that spread when you land. Tempo is made on N and S. Daily, Long and Ridge are made on S and W. Ease is made on W and O. Open is made only on O.

In a gait session we put three pairs on two lasts, so you can feel the width on the treadmill before you choose. If the last you need is not on the shelf, a special order takes 10 to 14 days.

pages.title: Lasts
pages.content:
Four lasts

Four lasts.

We stock four lasts: Narrow, Standard, Wide and Open toe. Widths are measured inside a US men's 9, and every house pair is built on at least one of them.

THE FOUR

Narrow to open toe

Forefoot width measured inside a US men’s 9: 94, 98, 103 and 108 mm. Every pair we sell is built on one or more of them.

Compare below

LAST N · 94 mm

Narrow

Narrow, code N, measures 94 mm across the forefoot inside a US men's 9. It is the last for low-volume feet and a narrow heel. Tempo is the pair we build on Narrow, and Tempo is also built on Standard, so the two can be compared in one visit. The row for Narrow shows Tempo: 6 mm drop, 30 mm stack at the heel, 225 g in US men's 9, $185, for faster days and races.

In the twenty minutes of Try, each pair gets about two minutes on the treadmill, filmed from the side and from behind. If Narrow holds the heel and another last feels better in the toes, that is what the last five minutes of the session are for. A special order for a different last takes 10 to 14 days. The deposit is $20, credited to the pair.

See pairs on N

LAST S · 98 mm

Standard

Standard, code S, measures 98 mm across the forefoot inside a US men's 9. It is the last for most feet. Daily, Long, Tempo and Ridge all come on Standard. Daily, Long and Ridge also come on Wide. Tempo also comes on Narrow. The Standard row shows Daily, PAIR 01, the everyday training shoe: 8 mm drop, 32 mm heel stack, 268 g in US men's 9, $145.

Long on Standard is the pair Jonah settled on after the side video showed his heel slipping in Tempo on Narrow. Long is $165, with a 6 mm drop, a 38 mm stack and a weight of 285 g. You can buy Standard from the shelf after a session, or order it later with the session code. We keep those notes for 12 months.

See pairs on S

LAST W · 103 mm

Wide

Wide, code W, measures 103 mm across the forefoot inside a US men's 9. It is for a high-volume foot or a wide midfoot. Daily, Long, Ridge and Ease come on Wide. The Wide row shows Ridge, PAIR 04, the trail shoe: 4 mm drop, 30 mm heel stack, 296 g in US men's 9, $160. Ama, 38, left on Ridge in Wide with a heel-lock lace set-up for a trail 50 km, then came back for the three-week re-check.

Daniel Osei runs the Saturday trail fittings. Ben Kowalski does the heel-lock in the workshop. That set-up is about 10 minutes and free. The re-check run is 20 minutes and free with a pair. Ease on Wide is the other high-volume option, at $125, when the day is for recovery or walking. Moulded insoles, if you want them with the pair, are $60 and take 30 minutes.

See pairs on W

LAST O · 108 mm

Open toe

Open toe, code O, measures 108 mm across the forefoot inside a US men's 9. It is for a wide forefoot and for toes that spread when you land. Ease comes on Wide and on Open toe. Open, PAIR 06, comes only on Open toe. The Open-toe row shows Open: 0 mm drop, 27 mm heel stack, 240 g in US men's 9, $150. Ease is PAIR 05, for recovery and walking: 4 mm drop, 34 mm stack, 252 g, $125.

Maren, 52, came back to running after ten years and moved from her old pair to Ease on the Open-toe last. She said, "my toes finally have room on the downhill." Under the four rows, the comparison is the same three facts for each last: the code, the inside width at US men's 9, and the pairs we build on it. N 94 mm, Tempo. S 98 mm, Daily, Long, Tempo, Ridge. W 103 mm, Daily, Long, Ridge, Ease.

O 108 mm, Ease and Open.

pages.title: Gait session
pages.content:
45 minutes, $40

Gait session

A gait session is 45 minutes on the shop treadmill, filmed from the side and from behind. The fee is $40, credited if you buy a pair within 30 days.

TALK · WATCH

Talk and Watch

Talk is the opening 10 minutes, off the belt. We ask what you run, how often you run, and what your current pair does well or badly. Watch is the next 10 minutes. You wear those current shoes on the treadmill at an easy pace. A camera films from the side and from behind. We look at where you land and how the foot rolls.

The lab view is low, near the ankle, with the belt and a small camera in the frame. Bring the shoes you are actually using. Doors open at 10:00 Tuesday to Friday and Sunday, and at 09:00 on Saturday. They close at 19:00 Tuesday to Friday, at 17:00 on Saturday and at 15:00 on Sunday. The first session of the day starts as the doors open.

At 09:30, before that, we check the treadmill belt and charge the camera.

Book a session

TRY · DECIDE

Try and Decide

Try fills 20 minutes. You run three pairs on two lasts, about two minutes in each pair, and we play the clips back side by side. Decide is the last 5 minutes. You can buy the pair in the shop, order it online later from your session notes, or special-order another last or size. Notes stay on file for 12 months, attached to your session code. A special order takes 10 to 14 days.

The deposit is $20, and it is credited to the pair. Leave with a pair and the three-week re-check run is free: 20 minutes. Ben Kowalski can mould insoles in the workshop in 30 minutes for $60, or set up lacing and a heel lock in about 10 minutes at no charge. The six pairs you might be choosing among are Daily $145, Long $165, Tempo $185, Ridge $160, Ease $125 and Open $150.

How ordering works

THE FOUR PARTS

Forty-five minutes, four parts

A gait session is 45 minutes and costs $40. The $40 is credited if you buy a pair within 30 days. The order of the hour does not change. Talk is 10 minutes. Watch is 10 minutes. Try is 20 minutes. Decide is 5 minutes. Priya Raman leads the sessions and trains every fitter on that script, so a visit with Noor Haddad, Daniel Osei or Lucía Ferreira follows the same clock. You may also book a quick fit, 20 minutes with no treadmill, at no charge. Sessions start on the hour. The last start is 18:00 Tuesday to Friday, 16:00 on Saturday and 14:00 on Sunday. Monday the shop is closed. Book on +1 (303) 555-0142 or hello@kakeru-run.example.

PRICES

  • Gait session$40Credited if you buy a pair within 30 days.

All prices →

QUESTIONS

Before you book

What do I get for the $40?

The $40 covers one 45-minute gait session in the shop at 2140 Canyon Row. You get time on our treadmill, video from the side and from behind, and three pairs tried on two lasts. The four parts are Talk 10 minutes, Watch 10 minutes, Try 20 minutes and Decide 5 minutes. Watch is in your current shoes at an easy pace. Try is two minutes in each pair, played back so you can see the clips together. If you buy a pair within 30 days, we credit the $40 to that pair. The price is the same one printed on the home page and on the prices page. Quick fit is a separate booking, 20 minutes, free, and it does not use the treadmill. Moulded insoles are separate again, at $60 for 30 minutes.

Do I have to leave with a pair?

You do not have to buy at the end of the five minutes. Decide means exactly three choices: buy now, order online later from your session notes, or special-order another last or size. If you buy within 30 days, the $40 session fee is credited to the pair. If you wait longer than 30 days, the session fee stays as paid and the pair is at its own price. Daily is $145, Long $165, Tempo $185, Ridge $160, Ease $125, Open $150. The notes themselves are kept for 12 months, so the later order can still follow what you tried. Hana Lindgren on the orders desk handles that online order, the special order and any return. A return is 30 days, and the pair needs to be unworn.

What is a quick fit?

A quick fit is 20 minutes and free. It does not use the treadmill, the side camera or the rear camera. It is the visit for checking a last and a size when you already know which of the six pairs you want. The full gait session remains 45 minutes and $40 when you want the video and the three-pair comparison. Sessions of either kind start on the hour while the shop is open: Tuesday to Friday 10:00 to 19:00, Saturday 09:00 to 17:00, Sunday 10:00 to 15:00. Monday is closed. The last gait session starts at 18:00 Tuesday to Friday, 16:00 on Saturday and 14:00 on Sunday. Lucía Ferreira covers evenings and Sunday. Daniel Osei runs the Saturday trail fittings. Call +1 (303) 555-0142 or write to hello@kakeru-run.example and name the hour.

When can a session start?

Gait sessions start on the hour, and only inside the hours the doors are open. Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday the shop is open 10:00 to 19:00, and the last session starts at 18:00. Saturday the shop is open 09:00 to 17:00, and the last session starts at 16:00. Sunday the shop is open 10:00 to 15:00, and the last session starts at 14:00. Monday is closed. A session is 45 minutes, so the last start still finishes inside the day. The daily routine begins earlier: at 09:30 we check the treadmill belt and charge the camera, and at 10:00 the doors open for the first session. Evening runners are in around 17:00. At 19:00 the day's online orders go out to the carrier. Book the hour by phone or by the mail address on this page.

How long do you keep session notes?

We keep session notes for 12 months. The notes record what you told us in the first 10 minutes, what the side and rear video showed, and which three pairs on which two lasts you tried. Your session code is how you order online later without repeating the visit. Hana Lindgren matches the code at the orders desk. After you have the code, you can buy from the six pairs at the prices already set: $145, $165, $185, $160, $125 and $150. Shipping in the US is a flat $8, free over $120, and we ship in 1 to 2 business days. A special order, if the notes say you need another last or size, still takes 10 to 14 days and a $20 deposit credited to the pair. The code does not change those lead times.

What is the three-week re-check?

The three-week re-check run is 20 minutes, and it is free when you have bought a pair. It is a return visit on the same treadmill, booked on the hour like any other session. Ama, 38, came back for hers after leaving on Ridge in Wide with a heel-lock lace set-up, for a trail 50 km. The heel-lock itself is a separate 10-minute set-up in the workshop with Ben Kowalski, and that set-up is free. Moulded insoles, if they come up at the same visit, are $60 and take 30 minutes. The re-check does not replace the original 45-minute session, and it is not the quick fit. Book it with the shop at +1 (303) 555-0142 or hello@kakeru-run.example. Name the pair you bought so the fitter has it ready. Last starts remain 18:00, 16:00 on Saturday and 14:00 on Sunday.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Since 2014

About

Kakeru Run is a running-shoe fitting shop in Boulder, opened in 2014 by Noor Haddad and Tomas Varga. Seven people work the floor, the workshop and the orders desk.

FOUNDERS

Opened in 2014

Noor Haddad is founder and head fitter. She opened Kakeru Run in 2014 after years of club running and shop-floor fitting. The name is kakeru, to run, to dash. Tomas Varga is co-founder. He looks after lasts and stock: he chooses the four lasts and the six pairs, and he works with the partner factory. The lasts are Narrow, Standard, Wide and Open toe.

The pairs are Daily, Long, Tempo, Ridge, Ease and Open. The shop is at 2140 Canyon Row, Boulder, Colorado 80302, USA. A visit starts from how you land. We watch that first, on the treadmill, then show you the pairs worth trying. Most people begin with the 45-minute gait session. Priya Raman trains every fitter on the script so the hour is the same whoever is in the room.

Visit the shop

A DAY AT THE SHOP

A day at the shop

This is the daily routine. At 09:30 we check the treadmill belt and charge the camera. At 10:00 the doors open and the first session starts. At noon we restock from the back wall of lasts. At 17:00 the evening runners come in after work. At 19:00 the day's online orders go to the carrier. Tuesday to Friday the doors are open 10:00 to 19:00. Saturday is 09:00 to 17:00.

Sunday is 10:00 to 15:00. Monday is closed. Gait sessions start on the hour. The last start is 18:00 Tuesday to Friday, 16:00 on Saturday and 14:00 on Sunday. Lucía Ferreira takes the evening sessions and Sunday. Daniel Osei runs the Saturday trail fittings.

The room itself is a long white wall of shoes on shallow shelves, the treadmill in the middle, and daylight from a large window.

WORKSHOP

Moulded insoles, 30 minutes

Ben Kowalski runs the workshop: moulded insoles, lacing and heel-lock set-ups, in a room next to the fitting floor.

THE TEAM

The seven of us

Noor Haddad, founder and head fitter, opened the shop in 2014 after years of club running and shop-floor fitting. Tomas Varga, co-founder for lasts and stock, chooses the four lasts and the six pairs and works with the partner factory. Priya Raman, gait session lead, trains every fitter on the session script. Daniel Osei, fitter for trail, runs the Saturday trail fittings. Lucía Ferreira, fitter, covers evenings and Sunday sessions. Ben Kowalski, in the workshop, moulds insoles and sets up lacing and heel locks. Hana Lindgren, on the orders desk, looks after online orders, special orders and returns. Insoles are $60 for 30 minutes. Lacing and a heel-lock set-up are free and take about 10 minutes. Those two workshop jobs sit with Ben. Returns, the 30-day unworn window, sit with Hana.

pages.title: Ordering
pages.content:
Three ways

Ordering

Order in the shop after a session, online with your session code, or by special order when you need another last or size. Notes from a session are kept for 12 months.

ORDER

Three ways to order

There are three ways to take a pair. In the shop, after a session, you buy it at the bench if your size and last are on the wall. Online, you order with your session code, and the notes behind that code are kept for 12 months. A special order is the third way, when you need another last or another size: 10 to 14 days, with a $20 deposit credited to the pair.

Hana Lindgren watches online orders, special orders and returns from the orders desk. The house line she is ordering from is Daily at $145, Long at $165, Tempo at $185, Ridge at $160, Ease at $125 and Open at $150. Tomas Varga chooses those six pairs and the four lasts, and he works with the partner factory. You can start from any of the three ways.

The prices do not change between them.

See the pairs

01 · IN STORE

After a session

Take your pair home the same day.

02 · ONLINE

With your session code

Notes are kept 12 months; order when you are ready.

03 · SPECIAL ORDER

Another last or size

10–14 days, $20 deposit credited to the pair.

SESSION CODE

Your session code

The session code points at the notes from your 45 minutes. Those notes hold what you run, how often, what your current pair does well or badly, the side and rear video, and the three pairs on two lasts you tried for two minutes each. We keep the notes for 12 months.

When you order online, the code is how the desk matches you to that visit, so the last on the order is the last you ran in. The gait session itself is $40, credited if you buy a pair within 30 days. A quick fit, 20 minutes with no treadmill, is free if you only need the size checked.

Place the order from the shoes list once you have the code, or call +1 (303) 555-0142 and read the code to Hana. The mail for the same desk is hello@kakeru-run.example.

SHIPPING AND RETURNS

Shipping, returns and the deposit

Inside the United States, shipping is a flat $8. It is free when the order is over $120. We ship in 1 to 2 business days. At 19:00, as the last step of the daily routine, the day's online orders go to the carrier. Returns are accepted for 30 days on unworn pairs. If the only running you have done in the pair was on our treadmill, the pair still counts as unworn.

A special order keeps the $20 deposit, credited to the pair, and the 10 to 14 day wait. The deposit is not the shipping fee. Shipping is calculated on its own, $8 unless the order is over $120. Questions about an order already placed go to the same desk, by phone or by hello@kakeru-run.example.

The shop address, if you would rather collect after a session, is 2140 Canyon Row, Boulder, Colorado 80302.

Back to the shoes →

pages.title: Customer stories
pages.content:
Customers

Stories from the fitting room

Stories from the fitting room sit next to short shop notes. Maren, Jonah and Ama are the three visits we have written up, in their own words only where we quote them.

STORY

Maren, 52

Maren is 52. She came back to running after ten years. During the visit she moved from her old pair to Ease on the Open-toe last. Ease is PAIR 05, for recovery and walking, priced at $125. It is built on Wide and Open toe, with a 4 mm drop, a 34 mm stack at the heel and a weight of 252 g in US men's 9.

Open toe measures 108 mm across the forefoot in that size, for a wide forefoot and for toes that spread on landing. Wide, the other last Ease comes on, measures 103 mm. Maren said, "my toes finally have room on the downhill." Her story is filed under Stories. The session she had was the usual 45 minutes: talk, watch, try, decide.

The Open-toe last was one of the two lasts in the twenty minutes of Try.

STORY

Jonah, 31

Jonah is 31. He came for his first marathon. He tried Tempo on the Narrow last. Tempo is PAIR 03, for faster days and races, $185, built on Narrow and Standard, with a 6 mm drop, a 30 mm heel stack and a weight of 225 g in US men's 9. Narrow measures 94 mm across the forefoot. The side video showed his heel slipping. He settled on Long on the Standard last.

Long is PAIR 02, for long runs, $165, built on Standard and Wide, with a 6 mm drop, a 38 mm stack and a weight of 285 g. Standard measures 98 mm. The side camera and the rear camera are what Watch and Try are for: an easy pace, then the pairs played back side by side. His story is tagged road. The picture with it is the Long pair, the shoe he left on.

STORY

Ama, 38

Ama is 38. She came in for a trail 50 km. She left on Ridge on the Wide last, with a heel-lock lace set-up, and she came back for the three-week re-check. Ridge is PAIR 04, the trail pair, $160, on Standard and Wide. The drop is 4 mm. The stack at the heel is 30 mm. The weight is 296 g in US men's 9.

Wide measures 103 mm across the forefoot, for a high-volume foot or a wide midfoot. Ben Kowalski set the heel lock in the workshop. That work takes about 10 minutes and is free. The re-check run is 20 minutes and free with a pair. Daniel Osei runs the Saturday trail fittings for visits of this kind. Ama's story is tagged trail.

The picture is a runner on a gravel path in the early morning, seen from the side at a distance.

SHOP NOTES

Shop notes

The journal has two categories, Stories and Shop notes, and four tags: road, trail, lasts and session. Beside Maren, Jonah and Ama there are three shop notes. How we film a session follows the camera through the 10 minutes of Watch and the 20 minutes of Try, side and rear, at an easy pace.

Why four lasts sets out Narrow, Standard, Wide and Open toe, and the inside widths at US men's 9: 94 mm, 98 mm, 103 mm and 108 mm. Re-check after three weeks is about the 20-minute return visit that comes free with a pair, the same kind of hour Ama booked after Ridge. Priya Raman's session script is the thread through the filming note.

Tomas Varga's four lasts are the thread through the lasts note. Ben Kowalski's workshop is the thread through the re-check note, when a heel lock or a moulded insole is part of the return.

posts.title: Why four lasts
posts.excerpt: Kakeru Run keeps four lasts, measured inside a US men's 9, and every pair we sell is built on one of them.
posts.content:
Tomas Varga chooses the lasts. He is co-founder, and lasts and stock are his side of the shop. In 2014 he and Noor Haddad opened Kakeru Run at 2140 Canyon Row in Boulder. Noor had spent years in club running and on a shop floor, fitting people. Tomas took the forms the shoes are built on, and the six pairs we still sell. He works with the partner factory. The line has not grown past those six, and the lasts have not grown past four.

We measure the forefoot inside a US men's 9. Narrow, code N, is 94 mm. It is for low-volume feet and a narrow heel. Standard, code S, is 98 mm, and it is the last for most feet. Wide, code W, is 103 mm, for a high-volume foot or a wide midfoot. Open toe, code O, is 108 mm, for a wide forefoot and for toes that spread when you land. Those four numbers are the whole width chart. We do not publish a second chart for other sizes on this page. The fitter scales from the last you tried, in the size you wear, during the session.

Which pair sits on which last is fixed. Tempo, PAIR 03, is the only shoe on Narrow, and it is also made on Standard. It is for faster days and races: 6 mm drop, 30 mm stack at the heel, 225 g in US men's 9, $185. Daily, Long and Ridge share Standard and Wide. Daily is everyday training, 8 mm drop, 32 mm stack, 268 g, $145. Long is for long runs, 6 mm drop, 38 mm stack, 285 g, $165. Ridge is the trail pair, 4 mm drop, 30 mm stack, 296 g, $160. Ease sits on Wide and on Open toe, for recovery and walking: 4 mm drop, 34 mm stack, 252 g, $125. Open, PAIR 06, is the open-toe trainer and it comes only on O: 0 mm drop, 27 mm stack, 240 g, $150.

A gait session is where the two lasts meet. The hour is 45 minutes and costs $40, credited if you buy a pair within 30 days. Priya Raman trains every fitter on the same script. Ten minutes of talk about what you run, how often, and what the pair you arrived in does well or badly. Ten minutes on the treadmill in those shoes, at an easy pace, filmed from the side and from behind. Twenty minutes in three pairs on two lasts, about two minutes each, played back side by side. Five minutes to buy, to order later, or to special-order.

Jonah's visit is the clearest picture of why we keep two lasts in the room. He is 31, and he was in for his first marathon. He tried Tempo on Narrow. The side video showed his heel slipping. He settled on Long on Standard. The drop of those two pairs is the same 6 mm. The stack is not: Tempo is 30 mm at the heel, Long is 38 mm. The width is not either: 94 mm against 98 mm. The video is what made the choice, not a guess from the label.

Maren and Ama sit at the other end of the chart. Maren is 52. She had been away from running for ten years, and she moved from her old pair to Ease on the Open-toe last. She said her toes finally have room on the downhill. Open toe is the 108 mm last. Ama is 38. She came for a trail 50 km, left on Ridge in Wide, and added a heel-lock lace set-up. Wide is the 103 mm last. Ben Kowalski does that set-up in the workshop in about 10 minutes, at no charge. Ama came back for the three-week re-check, which is 20 minutes and free with a pair.

If the last you need is not on the wall, Hana Lindgren places a special order from the orders desk. The wait is 10 to 14 days. The deposit is $20, credited to the pair. Session notes, including the last you already tried, are kept for 12 months under a session code, so the order can follow the visit. Shipping in the US is $8, free over $120, and the pair goes out in 1 to 2 business days.

The shop hours, if you want to stand on the lasts in person, are Tuesday to Friday 10:00 to 19:00, Saturday 09:00 to 17:00, and Sunday 10:00 to 15:00. Monday is closed. Sessions start on the hour. The last start is 18:00, 16:00 on Saturday, and 14:00 on Sunday.
